newsitem.title: USA: SEC seeks Grigsby campaign gift records in Calif..
newsitem.headline: SEC seeks Grigsby campaign gift records in Calif..

text.p: A Securities and Exchange Commission official in Florida has asked California regulators for campaign contribution information about the former chairman of investment banking firm Grigsby Brandford & Co. Inc.

An official in the SEC Miami office asked the California Fair Political Practices Commission for information about Calvin Grigsby, who resigned as chairman of the firm earlier this month, government sources in California said Wednesday.
The move suggests that SEC staff in Miami has launched a probe of bond deals in Dade County, Fla., involving Grigsby.
Grigsby Brandford & Co. is one of the largest minority-owned investment banking firms in the United States. Grigsby did not return phone messages on Wednesday.
According to published reports, Grigsby has hired high-profile defence attorney Johnnie Cochran to represent him. Cochran, who successfully defended O.J. Simpson, was unavailable for comment.
Charles Senatore, the SEC's regional director in Miami, declined to comment. An SEC official in California also declined to comment.

The SEC official in Miami specifically asked the California Fair Political Practices Commission for a copy of a recent settlement between the commission and Grigsby. The SEC also asked the commission if it had any information about campaign contributions by Grigsby to Florida public officials.
The California commission sent a copy of the settlement to the SEC in Miami and told the SEC official that the commission does not have jurisdiction over out-of-state contributions.
The Miami Herald newspaper reported last week that Grigsby resigned after federal prosecutors from Miami interviewed him in California about Dade County bond deals.

His departure also came a week after the California Fair Political Practices Commission disclosed that Grigsby paid a $5,000 fine for making campaign contributions in California without full and complete disclosure.

The commission alleged that Grigsby made campaign contributions totalling $11,500 in the first half of 1993. During the second half of 1993, Fiscal Funding Co. Inc. and other entities controlled by Grigsby made campaign contributions totalling $42,000.

The commission said Grigsby and Fiscal Funding failed to file timely major donor campaign statements reporting these contributions. Grigsby is a 50 percent owner and controling partner of Fiscal Funding, an equipment leasing company.
The campaign contributions outlined by the California commission were made before rules were enacted nationwide to curb contributions in the municipal finance industry.

The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's Rule G-37 was enacted in April 1994. It bars municipal dealers that make contributions to issuer clients from doing business for two years with those governments.
The California Fair Political Practices Commission, based in Sacramento, Calif., enforces state rules that deal with political contributions and conflicts of interest.
